mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.0%) relative to historical averages compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek yield in equities.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0% (historical 50th percentile), or Rank IC over last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 6.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 6.0, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC over last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in housing starts (HOUST > 950) and retail sales (RSAFS > 430000) indicates robust consumer demand, supporting corporate revenue growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: doc:Consumer Spending and Housing Market Report
failure_condition: When HOUST > 950 and RSAFS > 430000, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC for interaction term over last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%), rising inflation erodes real corporate profits and prompts Federal Reserve tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC over last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 signals manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate earnings growth and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC over last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A strong housing market (HOUST > 950) indicates robust consumer confidence and spending, supporting corporate revenue growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 950, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC over last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in 3 months), strong employment growth supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in 3 months, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC over last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading above 2.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting Federal Reserve rate hikes that compress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC over last 5 years is below 0.05.
